description: Field definitions for a contributed signal. This file is the single source of truth: docs/contribute.js renders the form from it and scripts/ingest_submission.py validates against it, so a field added here reaches both sides at once.
conditionSyntax: A condition is {"field": <id>, "in": [<values>]}. A field is shown when its showWhen condition passes, and is required when required is true, or when required is a condition that passes. Absent showWhen means always shown.

sections.title: What kind of signal is this?
sections.blurb: The library splits on single-carrier versus multi-carrier first, then on whether the waveform is defined by a published standard. Everything after this follows from these three answers.

fields.label: Signal class
fields.help: Multi-carrier signals have an inherent bandwidth. Single-carrier signals are a symbol sequence whose bandwidth only becomes meaningful once a sample rate is chosen.

fields.label: Signal family
fields.help: The grouping this waveform belongs to in the browser. Reuse an existing family name where one fits.

fields.label: Is the waveform defined by a published standard?

options.label: Yes — it follows a standard's numerology
No — it is a custom or generic waveform

sections.title: Standard parameters
sections.blurb: Enough to reproduce the waveform from the standard's own terms.

fields.label: Standard
fields.help: Name it the way the library already does where possible: WiFi4 for 802.11n, WiFi5 for 802.11ac, WiFi6 for 802.11ax, WiFi7 for 802.11be.

fields.label: Release or amendment
fields.help: Optional, but it settles which version of the numerology was used.

fields.label: MCS index
fields.help: The modulation and coding scheme index as the standard numbers it.

fields.label: Guard interval / cyclic prefix
fields.help: Meaningful for OFDM standards. Leave blank if it does not apply.

fields.label: Spatial streams
fields.help: The library's own signals are all single-stream (SISO).

fields.label: Data symbols per packet
fields.help: Packet airtime is what makes PAPR comparable across MCS, so record it if you know it.

fields.label: Inter-packet idle time
fields.help: Idle samples between packets. The library uses 16 us and excludes them from the PAPR mean.

sections.title: Waveform parameters
sections.blurb: What the waveform is, when no standard defines it.

fields.label: Modulation
fields.help: Write QAM orders the way the library does: 64-QAM, 1024-QAM.

fields.label: Occupied bandwidth
fields.help: For an RRC-shaped single-carrier signal this is symbol rate x (1 + roll-off).

fields.label: Symbol rate
fields.help: Single-carrier only. Sample rate divided by the oversampling ratio.

fields.label: Pulse-shaping filter
fields.help: The library's single-carrier signals are all RRC-shaped at 4x oversampling.

fields.label: Filter roll-off (alpha)
fields.help: The library ships 0.05, 0.15, 0.25, 0.35 and 0.45.

fields.label: Filter description
fields.placeholder: What the filter is, and how it was designed.

fields.label: Symbols in the file
fields.help: The library's single-carrier signals come in 100, 1k, 10k, 100k and 1M symbol lengths.

sections.title: Sampling and file format
sections.blurb: How the numbers in the file map onto time. Everything downstream — resampling for an instrument, comparing PAPR against the library curves — depends on getting this right.

fields.label: Sample rate
fields.help: The rate the file is written at, not the instrument you intend to play it on.

fields.label: Oversampling ratio
fields.help: Sample rate divided by the Nyquist rate of the underlying signal. Every signal in the library today is 4x.

fields.label: Sample format

options.label: Delimited text, one I,Q pair per line

fields.help: Detected from the file where possible. Correct it if the detection is wrong — every later reader trusts this field.

options.label: Little-endian (x86, and what the library writes)

sections.title: Hua Wang PA survey cross-reference
sections.blurb: If this waveform was used to measure a PA that appears in the Georgia Tech / Hua Wang PA survey, recording the link here ties the waveform to the published PA result. That link is the piece normally missing when comparing PA numbers across labs.

fields.label: Is the PA this signal was used with in the Hua Wang PA survey?
Survey edition or access date
fields.help: The survey is revised over time, so the row you are pointing at is only unambiguous alongside the edition you read.

fields.label: Survey entry / row identifier
fields.help: Whatever identifies the row in the edition you used.

fields.label: DOI of the paper
fields.patternHelp: A bare DOI, starting with 10. and no https://doi.org/ prefix.
fields.help: The most durable join key: survey rows get renumbered between editions, DOIs do not.

fields.label: PA technology
fields.help: Helps disambiguate when one paper reports several PAs.

fields.label: How certain is the match?

options.label: Exact — this is the waveform the paper used
Reconstructed — rebuilt from the parameters the paper states
Representative — same standard and settings, not the original file

fields.help: Most papers do not describe their test waveform precisely enough to reconstruct exactly. Saying so here keeps the cross-reference from reading as stronger evidence than it is.

fields.label: Cross-reference notes
fields.placeholder: Which measurement in the paper this waveform corresponds to, and anything that had to be assumed.

sections.title: Provenance and licence
sections.blurb: Who made the waveform and on what terms it can be redistributed. A signal whose licence is unclear cannot be published.

fields.label: Contact (email or GitHub handle)
fields.help: Optional, and it will be visible in the public issue. Leave blank if you would rather it were not.

fields.label: Generated with
fields.placeholder: MATLAB R2023b WLAN Toolbox, GNU Radio 3.10, ...
fields.help: Tool and version. Two toolchains claiming the same standard do not always produce the same waveform.

fields.label: How it was generated
fields.placeholder: Script, settings, and anything non-obvious about how the file was produced.

fields.label: Licence
fields.help: The repository is MIT licensed; either of the first two lets a contributed waveform sit alongside it without friction.

fields.label: I have the right to publish this waveform under the licence above, and it contains no proprietary or export-controlled content.
